title: Show linked procedure progress on living optimization reports
description:
As an operator, I want a living optimization Report to show its linked Procedure Task summary and a plain-language run identity, so that I can understand what kind of run it is and what is happening without interpreting internal scope selectors.

Out of scope: changing Task lifecycle ownership, introducing new backend resources, or removing detailed scope evidence from the Report body.

Feature: Procedure-aware living Report header

Scenario: View a Report linked to a Procedure Task
Given a living optimization Report is linked to its Procedure Task
When an operator opens the Report
Then the page shows the standard Procedure Task visual summary
And the run type and lifecycle state are understandable at a glance
And raw scope selector syntax is not used as the primary subtitle or description

Scenario: View a Report without a linked Task
Given a Report has no linked Procedure Task
When an operator opens the Report
Then the Report remains readable
And the page does not show a broken Task summary

Scenario: Inspect exact scope
Given a living optimization Report has normalized scope evidence
When an operator needs execution details
Then the exact scope remains available in the Report evidence below the header

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Operator acceptance found that the Report subtitle and top description expose normalized selector wording and repeat lifecycle metadata instead of showing the established Procedure Task summary. Implementation will reuse the existing Task presentation, preserve exact scope in detailed evidence, and retain a graceful unlinked-Report fallback.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented the operator-facing correction without schema or infrastructure changes. New living Reports use purpose-oriented subtitles, the cover no longer repeats raw scope selectors or a duplicate current-phase line, and Report detail embeds the linked Procedure Task's standard compact stage/status visualization. Older Reports without a true Procedure Task remain readable and do not invent linkage. Evidence: 40 focused Python tests, 8 focused dashboard tests, dashboard frontend/backend typechecks, and diff checks pass. Fresh live acceptance remains pending behind the separately recorded agentless-runtime defect.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Live operator review found that the aggregate metric label 'Account inventory inspected' obscures its unit. The value counts scorecards, so the presentation should label it directly as 'Scorecards inspected'. Adding focused UI coverage before changing the component.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Changed the aggregate metric to the explicit unit label 'Scorecards inspected'. The focused component test now asserts the new label and rejects the old wording; dashboard frontend/backend typechecks pass. Live local-dashboard verification against the completed portfolio Report shows '56 Scorecards inspected' and no old label.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Live browser diagnosis found three nested vertical scrollers after embedding the Procedure Task; the Report cover was constrained to a 24-pixel-tall inner scroll box. Reworked the detail layout so the linked Procedure summary and Report cover share the existing outer detail-pane scroller. Focused tests and both dashboard typechecks pass. Live wheel verification on the completed Report moved the right pane from scrollTop 0 to 545 with a 396-pixel viewport over 2,722 pixels of content.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Extended the living optimization Report so operators can see how work was selected: every eligible score now has a stable rank; the Report states that ranking has no eligibility cutoff; the highlighted top-list boundary and reviewed-disagreement value are explicit; and the separate semantic-diagnosis selection boundary is explained. Priority rows now carry feedback volume, disagreement rate, readiness, rationale, and next action. Workbook projections include rank and disagreement rate. Validation: 53 focused Python tests, the focused dashboard component test, and dashboard frontend/backend typechecks pass. Fresh account-wide live acceptance remains next.
